note: Fixture: a correct norm comparison for f_n(x)=x^n (sup norm 1, L1 norm 1/(n+1), non-equivalence concluded, finite-dimensional hypothesis named). Selected when all automatic checks pass.

object.summary: Both norms are computed correctly: $\|f_n\|_\infty = 1$ since $x^n$ is increasing on $[0,1]$ with value 1 at $x=1$, and $\|f_n\|_1 = \int_0^1 x^n\,dx = \tfrac{1}{n+1}$. The conclusion is drawn correctly: the ratio $\|f_n\|_\infty / \|f_n\|_1 = n+1$ is unbounded, so no constant $C$ satisfies $\|f\|_\infty \le C\|f\|_1$ on $C([0,1])$, and the two norms are not equivalent. The contrast with finite dimensions is stated with the right hypothesis.

checks.comment: Supremum identified as 1 with justification (monotonicity on [0,1]).
Unbounded ratio used to refute the existence of a comparison constant in the direction that fails.
Finite dimensionality named as the hypothesis behind norm equivalence; its failure here is the point.

strengths: The direction of the inequality that fails is identified explicitly rather than asserting non-equivalence vaguely.
object.nextStep: Ask whether the reverse inequality $\|f\|_1 \le C\|f\|_\infty$ holds on $C([0,1])$, and with which constant; then ask whether $(C([0,1]), \|\cdot\|_1)$ is complete.
